To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the nuclear spectral functions computed with the realistic Argonne V18 and Bonn B nucleon-nucleon potentials provide a reasonable description of the measured separation energies, and (2) the binding effects on the nuclear response functions are large, of order of 5-10%, and are comparable in size to the effect of nuclear shadowing
the nuclear spectral function computed with realistic interactions can be used to estimate the binding correction to lepton-nuclear scattering, and that these corrections are significant.

the binding corrections to DIS in nuclei are significant, that the corrections are large and negative, and that the corrections depend on the momentum transfer, the energy transfer, the nuclear mass, and the isotope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear structure of nuclei and the role of the nucleon-nucleon interaction in this structure.
the development and application of the theory of nuclear structure and the nuclear force to problems of current interest.
the study of the nuclear spectral function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding corrections are significant and must be considered in any analysis of data.
the use of realistic spectral functions leads to a reduction of the binding correction to the cross section by a factor of 3 to 5, depending on the nucleus and the kinematics.
the binding corrections to deep-inelastic scattering are large and that the spectral function method provides the most reliable estimate of the magnitude of these corrections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding corrections to deep inelastic scattering can be computed reliably using realistic spectral functions.
the binding corrections are not large enough to change the interpretation of the experimental results.
the binding correction to inclusive electron scattering off nuclei is of the same order of magnitude as the correction due to the nuclear Fermi motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear binding effects are significant and cannot be ignored in the analysis of lepton-nuclei deep inelastic scattering data.
binding effects are not small, and that they should not be ignored.
the nuclear spectral functions should be used in place of the Fermi gas spectral function in calculations of binding corrections.
